newsitem.title: USA: Conn. U.S. Sen. Dodd says plans nuke legislation.
newsitem.headline: Conn. U.S. Sen. Dodd says plans nuke legislation.

text.p: Connecticut U.S. Sen. Christopher Dodd said Wednesday he plans to introduce legislation which would provide funds to towns and cities affected by decommissioning of nuclear power plants.
Dodd, a Democrat, said the Distressed Community Support Act of 1997 would allow a portion of the fines levied by federal regulators to be routed back to communities affected by the dismantling.
The communities could use the funds to lessen the impact and promote economic development and recovery.
"Those who are most affected by decommissioning should be assisted and guided down the road to economic recovery," Dodd said in a statement.

Dodd and Economic Development Administration officials on Wednesday invited the town of Haddam, Conn., to apply for grant money of up to $40,000 to help recover from the closing of the Connecticut Yankee nuclear plant.
The 582-megawatt Connecticut Yankee, operated by Northeast Utilities, was permanently closed last December after safety concerns had idled it since July 1996.
Northeast has said the plant's dismantling could cost about $425 million.
Northeast said earlier this month it will pay a $650,000 fine proposed by the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission for past violations at Connecticut Yankee.
